messages:
priya: Customer reports SSE streams ending abruptly after ~60s when routed through an ALB in front of our hosted API. They see partial output (truncated JSON) and client reconnects; sometimes the reconnect resumes where the client left off and sometimes it gets duplicate tokens. Happening across multiple regions but only for customers on ALB with TLS termination.

alex: Any request IDs or sample logs? Is this the same bucket as the previous keepalive issues? :thinking_face:

priya: Request id: req_0a7b3c9f. Repro steps they gave:

1) Open an EventSource (JS) to our /v1/stream endpoint
2) Let it idle for ~55-70s (no server-sent heartbeat from client)
3) The client gets a truncated last chunk, connection closes, then client reconnects with Last-Event-ID and gets a partial continuation or duplicate tokens.

Curl repro they used (simplified):
```bash
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=..."
```

Headers from the capture (client -> ALB -> us):
```
:method: GET
:scheme: https
:authority: api.redwood.ai
accept: text/event-stream
authorization: Bearer **redacted**
user-agent: CustomAgent/1.2
```

They also attached a tcpdump showing an ALB FIN to the backend right after the last chunk body is flushed.

maya: ALB default idle timeout is 60s, so that lines up. Also note ALB does HTTP/2 on frontside and HTTP/1.1 to backends. HTTP/2 session resumption + TLS session ticket rotation can change which underlying TCP connection is used and may trigger ALB to close idle backend connections. If backend is mid-stream and we rely on a long-lived conn, ALB can send RST/FIN to backend while frontend still has client connection open.

jonah: Do we see any server logs (our side) showing socket close while writing chunked body? If we flushed a final partial chunk then the FIN from ALB could truncate the last event. Also need to differentiate between application-level heartbeat vs TCP-level keepalive.

priya: Attached server log snippet: (trimmed)
```
[INFO] req_0a7b3c9f stream start
[DEBUG] flush chunk 1 (tokens 0-63)
[DEBUG] flush chunk 2 (tokens 64-127)
[WARN] write failed: broken pipe
[INFO] req_0a7b3c9f stream end (client disconnect)
```

alex: Thanks. Two immediate axes: (1) connection-level: ALB idle timeout / HTTP/2->1.1 mapping; (2) app-level: add frequent SSE heartbeat comments so ALB sees activity on frontside and keeps backend conn alive. Also check if ALB connection draining / deregistration events happened.

maya: Quick mitigations we can suggest to customers:
- Increase ALB idle timeout to >120s if they can control it.
- Ensure the client sends periodic pings or server emits a comment heartbeat every 15-20s, e.g., ":heartbeat

" to keep ALB backend conn active.
- Turn off HTTP/2 between client and ALB (Cloud provider setting) if streaming fragility persists — this forces 1:1 mapping of connections and avoids HTTP/2 multiplexing-induced reuse.
- If using Nginx/Cloudflare in front of ALB, set `proxy_buffering off` / `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and disable response buffering.

jonah: For our side: add robust handling for partial flushes so we don't consider truncated chunk a completed inference. We should persist output token cursor so if client reconnects with Last-Event-ID we can resume consistently rather than duplicate tokens. Also log upstream close reason if available (tcp_info).

priya: Customer says they use a Fetch/EventSource polyfill that re-opens with Last-Event-ID. In some reconnects they got duplicate tokens — that suggests our resume logic relies on perfect final-chunk semantics. If ALB truncates the last chunk mid-event we currently mark as completed and move cursor forward.

alex: Action items:
- @maya please check ALB metrics for that account around req_0a7b3c9f timestamp (2034567890), look for active/idle connection closures and target health events.
- @maya/@jonah can we add more defensive logging around socket write errors and capture `SO_ERROR`/`tcp_info` when a write fails?
- @maya please confirm if we recently changed TLS ticket rotation or if deploy-bot shows ALB config updates.

deploy-bot: ALB config change detected for prod cluster: `idle_timeout` set to 60 -> 60 (no change) at 2034565000 by infra/auto-scaler. TLS ticket rotation policy updated 2034564000 (rotate every 5m).

maya: I queried the ALB access and target logs: multiple backend connection resets at ~2034567888-2034567902 coincident with the request. No target deregistration events. TLS ticket rotation value might be relevant — frequent ticket rotation can cause session resumption to prefer different backend connections. I'll pull tcpdumps and the ALB's ELB logs for that timeframe.

priya: Customer follow-up: they tried adding a client-side 10s heartbeat and saw a big drop in incidents. But they can't change ALB config. They asked if we can add server-side heartbeat by default for streaming responses for hosted customers behind ALBs. Any performance/cost impacts?

jonah: Small token overhead for heartbeat comments, negligible. But downstream customers using strict parsers might choke on extra comment lines — we should make it opt-in per account or detect ALB via `via` headers? Alternatively add a `heartbeat_interval` query param/streaming header.

alex: Good plan. Let's do short-term recommendations to the customer: (1) add 10-15s client heartbeats or accept server-sent comments (we can enable temporarily for their account), (2) if they can, increase ALB idle timeout >120s, (3) avoid HTTP/2 frontends if possible.

priya: I'll reply to customer with repro guidance, suggested mitigations, and ask permission to enable server heartbeats on their tenant while we implement resume hardening.

maya: I'll upload ALB tcpdumps + ELB logs to the ticket and open an internal ticket for resume/cursor robustness. Also will audit whether TLS ticket rotation frequency is too aggressive for streaming workloads.

jonah: For the resume fix: proposed server-side algorithm: only advance token cursor once we successfully ACK a final newline-delimited SSE event boundary, and on TCP write error mark stream as truncated so reconnect resume uses overlapping token window to dedupe. We'll need to coordinate with the SDK team to handle dedupe reliably.

priya: Sounds good. I'll keep updates in the support ticket. Thanks all :pray: 

ops-bot: Incident note created: SUP-203456-ALB-SSE, linked ticket: https://redwood.support/tickets/203456 (automated).
